ov: The smooth-head blobfish, a deep-sea fish of the waters off Australia, Tasmania and New Zealand, usually under 30 cm long. Its flesh is a jelly slightly less dense than water, so instead of swimming much it floats just above the seabed and eats what drifts past.
rg: Deep water off mainland Australia, Tasmania and New Zealand, 600–1,200 m down.
df: Edible matter that floats in front of it, such as deep-sea crustaceans.
fx: It lives where the pressure is 60 to 120 times that at sea level, too deep for a swim bladder to work well.
The famous photo of "Mr Blobby" shows a related species, Psychrolutes microporos.
